name: Kura
notes: The homepage says Kura is backed by Y Combinator and lists client-side encryption, stealth browsers, proxy management, credential handling and audit trails. The documentation says the Recursion agent executes each plain-language instruction on the web page in real time and adds the matching blocks to a workflow; Action blocks click, type, press keys and refresh, go back or open, close and switch tabs, alongside navigation, extraction, checkpoint (natural-language assertion), for-loop and conditional blocks. Action and navigation blocks cache the elements or URLs they used and fall back to full reasoning when a cached step fails. A deployed agent gets synchronous and asynchronous API endpoints. The benchmarks page reports 87.0% on 602 of WebVoyager's 643 tasks (41 removed as impossible, booking, login or print tasks) and 90% against 56% for Anthropic's computer-use demo on 50 sampled tasks, for a hierarchical agent of planners, an executor and critics that runs mainly on GPT-4o; these figures are publisher-reported and were not reproduced. Availability and reliability were not independently tested.
summary: Enterprise browser-agent builder whose Recursion agent runs plain-language steps on the live page and saves them as workflow blocks (actions, navigation, extraction, checks) with cached selectors, deployable as APIs.
